key_insight: CREW replaces fixed multi-agent workflows with reinforcement-learned coordination, letting LLM agents dynamically choose how to collaborate when generating related work sections.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for building cheaper, more adaptable multi-agent LLM systems for scientific writing and other structured generation tasks that benefit from autonomous role selection.
method: Agents autonomously choose actions such as Retrieve, Disseminate, Compose, and Critique.
Coordination is optimized with Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO).
The framework bypasses rigid heuristic pipelines in favor of learned collaboration policies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive evaluation on a standard RWG benchmark, with improved quality over strong baselines and lower token cost.
watch_item: Performance depends on training stable multi-agent policies, so results may be sensitive to reward design and benchmark-specific behavior.
paper_title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation
